text: Serbian bollards might look like Austria/Slovenia bollards but reflector will be always off-center. They have couple other designs but reflector will be always off-center.

clues.title: Pedestrian sign: Switch-up Serbia
text: Serbia has 2 different pedestrian signs. **Horizontal Zebra stripe**: Austria, Belgium, Greece, Poland, Serbia. > **No hat + rounded, non-detailed guy**: Serbia. OR **5 Zebra stripes + rounded guy + no belt + white/silver border + no blue corners**: Serbia, and Slovenia.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Bollards
text: Serbia has a few bollard designs, however most of them will have an off-centred reflector.
The bollards are usually flat, with no depth to them.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Chevron: Chevrons
text: Serbia uses chevrons with a black arrow on a white background.
Within Europe, these chevrons can also be found in Slovenia, Montenegro and North Macedonia.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Google car: No Antenna
text: Most of the coverage in Serbia was taken by a Google car with no antenna.
Other than North Macedonia, almost all of central and eastern Europe has antenna coverage in Generation 3.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Guardrail: B-Type Guardrails
text: Serbia uses B-Profile guardrails exclusively.
North Macedonia does not use B-Profile guardrails.

text: Belgrade street signs have cyrillic and latin written on them, it also has a unique shield icon on the left which has the serbian flag colors in it.

clues.title: Language: Serbian
text: Serbian is the version of Serbo-Croatian official in Serbia. Serbian uses both the Cyrillic and Latin script, and most official road signs use both scripts. Croatian will never use Cyrillic, while Bosnian and Montenegrin might. These letters are unique to Serbo-Croatian (Cyrillic): **Ђ ђ** and **Ћ ћ**.

These letters are found in Serbo-Croatian and Macedonian: **Љ љ**, **Њ њ** and **Џ џ**. The **J** from Latin is also used in Cyrillic in these languages (in Bulgarian or Russian, **Й** is used instead).
The Serbo-Croatian word for street is **улица/ulica** (like most Slavic languages).

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
